risks: fenced_reachability visit_cap | medium | The function references 'visit_cap' which is not defined in this chunk; if it is a global or missing, behavior is undefined. | Check that 'visit_cap' is defined in the module or passed as argument.

fenced_dominance fraction denominator | medium | The comment says non-fenced candidates zero leads to 0.0, but code returns 0.0 if candidates empty. If candidates is empty, fraction=0.0 keeps guard ON as stated. | Confirm the guardrail logic expects 0.0 when no candidates.

handoff.purpose: Implements fenced_reachability and fenced_dominance functions for dependency graph analysis.

symbols.name: fenced_reachability
symbols.note: Checks if a relative path reaches a fenced node via reverse import edges; BFS with sorted frontier, cycle guard, visit_cap truncation.

symbols.name: fenced_dominance
symbols.note: Computes fraction of non-fenced modules that transitively feed a fenced module; multi-source BFS from fenced set over forward edges.

claims.text: ``hops`` >= 1 is the case the literal check cannot see: a leaf that a fenced module transitively depends on.
claims.why: The literal check is not defined in this chunk; cannot verify.

claims.text: Determinism is load-bearing (two processes must block the same edit with the same explanation): the frontier and every neighbour list are iterated sorted, first parent wins, and among fenced nodes found at the minimal hop level the lexicographically smallest is reported.
claims.why: Code uses sorted(frontier) and sorted(rev.get(node, ())) and hit[0] after sorting hit, ensuring deterministic order.

claims.text: Non-Python import edges are best-effort, so this OVER-reports. That is intended: a spurious escalation costs a Claude call, a missed one lets a 7B model write code a hardware interlock depends on. Do not "tighten" this.
claims.why: The nature of import edges (non-Python) is not observable in this chunk; over-reporting claim cannot be verified.

claims.text: Traverse from the CANONICAL spelling when there is one; an unknown path is still walked as given so a fenced-looking path is never let through merely for being absent from the graph.
claims.why: Code: rel = node or rel; node is canonical_node result; if node is None, rel (original) is used.

claims.text: DENOMINATOR CHOICE (deliberate): already-fenced modules are excluded. They are high-risk under the literal check today, so reachability changes nothing about them; counting them would measure "how safety-critical is this repo" instead of "how much NEW escalation does this feature add", and a repo that is 90% fenced would then trip the guardrail on the strength of files the feature never touches. What we want to bound is the delta.
claims.why: Code: candidates = sorted(nodes - fenced); fraction computed using len(escalated)/len(candidates).

claims.text: Computed as ONE multi-source BFS over the forward edges from the fenced set (a module reaches a fenced node in the reverse graph exactly when it is reachable from a fenced node in the forward graph), not V separate BFS runs -- the router calls this on every task and O(V*E) on a 7k-file repo is not something a fence may cost.
claims.why: Code: seen = set(fenced); frontier = sorted(fenced); while frontier: BFS using fwd edges; single BFS from all fenced nodes.

claims.text: No non-fenced candidates -> 0.0, which keeps the guard ON. A guardrail that fails toward "disable the fence" is the wrong failure.
claims.why: Code: if candidates else 0.0; fraction is 0.0 when candidates empty.
